payload.text:
I reviewed `dedupe-imports` against main (2 commits) and wouldn't merge it yet. The main feature doesn't work: lists that overlap don't get deduplicated. The tests still pass, because they never try the case that matters. I didn't edit anything.

**Blocker: `dedupe` compares objects instead of ids** (`src/dedupe.js`)
```js
return [...new Set(contacts)];
```
A `Set` only spots a duplicate when it's the exact same object in memory. But the README says overlapping imports produce the same id as *different objects*, and that "identity is the id, never object identity." So the duplicates this branch is meant to remove are exactly the ones it misses. I ran it to check:
```
mergeImports([{id:1,name:'Ada'}], [{id:1,name:'Ada'}])
→ [ { id: 1, name: 'Ada' }, { id: 1, name: 'Ada' } ]
```
`mergeImports` is wrong for the same reason. A possible fix that keeps the first contact seen for each id:
```js
function dedupe(contacts) {
  const seen = new Set();
  return contacts.filter((c) => !seen.has(c.id) && seen.add(c.id));
}
```

**Tests don't cover the real case** (`test/dedupe.test.js`)
- The only duplicate test uses the same object twice (`[a, a]`), and that's the one case the broken code handles. Add a test with two separate objects that share an id, and check that the first one is kept.
- There's no test for `mergeImports` at all. One test that merges two overlapping lists would have caught this.

**Minor**
- `byName` (`src/order.js`) is fine: it copies the list before sorting and treats a missing name as empty. It isn't called anywhere yet, so it isn't wired into the merge.
- The CHANGELOG, README and version bump to 2.2.0 are consistent with each other. They describe the intended behaviour, which the code doesn't deliver yet.

Once `dedupe` matches on id and there's a test with different objects sharing an id, this looks fine to merge.
